chapter: Fourteen years with Nat Cole and the recording sessions
title: Copying Oscar Moore's solos when Nat's records were remade
summary: Collins played the solos on remade Nat Cole records such as The Christmas Song, marked by a six-string chord at the end; live, Nat kept the solos.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: That's right, that's right. So this was -- here we go again -- this is why I never got a chance to do anything. But the money was good and so I just stayed there and made the money and, you know, sent my kids through school, you know, one of those things. But any way I did some -- I did have a couple of solos with Nat. Let's see, I did quite a few solos with him, but I had to -- now here's the funny thing. I would have to do -- to copy the solos that were played by Oscar, and Irving because we would record all these tunes over because Nat's voice, naturally as he got older, became deeper.
So they would do all of these tunes over, like the Christmas Song. Everyone things that they're hearing Oscar, but

that is me. And the only way I can tell that it's me because right on the very end I put a big chord on there where Oscar had a four string chord on there I put a six string chord on there, and this is the way that I can tell it's me.
Is that the only way you were allowed to deviate -- -- as much as you were allowed (inaudible).

I mean on recording, recording. Any playing to be done solo, during the show, Nat would take them on the piano. He would cut -- if we started out with me doing a solo and he had an arrangement made, he'd write me cut, because he would want to do, you know, all the solo and singing himself. Yeah.
